1.q: וַ⁠יַּקְהֵ֣ל דָּוִ֣יד אֶת־כָּל־שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַ⁠שְּׁבָטִ֣ים וְ⁠שָׂרֵ֣י הַ⁠מַּחְלְק֣וֹת הַ⁠מְשָׁרְתִ֪ים אֶת־הַ⁠מֶּ֟לֶךְ וְ⁠שָׂרֵ֣י הָ⁠אֲלָפִ֣ים וְ⁠שָׂרֵ֣י הַ⁠מֵּא֡וֹת וְ⁠שָׂרֵ֣י כָל־רְכוּשׁ־וּ⁠מִקְנֶה֩ ׀ לַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ וּ⁠לְ⁠בָנָ֜י⁠ו עִם־הַ⁠סָּרִיסִ֧ים וְ⁠הַ⁠גִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וּֽ⁠לְ⁠כָל־גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם
1.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put together the information that it was to **Jerusalem** that David **assembled** these **leaders**. Alternate translation: [And David assembled to Jerusalem all of the leaders of Israel, the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions serving the king and the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds and the officers of all of the property and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officials and the warriors and all of the warriors of valor]

2.note: David stood up to show respect for God, whose message to him he was about to relate to the assembly, and for the great assembly of these leaders. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And King David rose respectfully to his feet]

The words **brothers** and **people** together express a single idea. The word **brothers** tells what kind of **people** these were, that is, David’s kinsmen or fellow Israelites. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [my people who are my kinsmen]
See how you translated the same expression in 22:7. Alternate translation: [As for me, it was with my heart] or [As for me, it was my desire]

David is using the possessive form to describe a **house** (that is, a temple) that would be characterized by being a place where the **Box** of **Yahweh** would **rest**, that is, no longer move from place to place. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a permanent temple]

David is speaking as if the **house** or temple he wanted to build would actually have been a **footstool** for God’s **feet**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. See the further discussion of this image in the introduction to this chapter. Alternate translation: [and as a place where our God would be especially present]

3.q: וְ⁠הָ⁠אֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔⁠י לֹא־תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִ⁠שְׁמִ֑⁠י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְ⁠דָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [But God told me that I would not build a house for his name, for I had been a man of battles and had shed blood.’]

3.q: לֹא־תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִ⁠שְׁמִ֑⁠י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְ⁠דָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since you have been a man of battles and you have shed blood, you shall not build a house for my name]
See how you translated the similar expression “a man of war” in 18:10. Alternate translation: [you have fought many battles]
See how you translated the similar expression in 22:08. Alternate translation: [and have killed many people]

4.note: Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an elaboration. Alternate translation: [You see,]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and in the house of Judah, he chose the house of my father]

5.q: כִּ֚י רַבִּ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים נָ֥תַן לִ֖⁠י יְהוָ֑ה
5.note: David is providing background information to help readers understand what he says next. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

5.q: כִּ֚י רַבִּ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים נָ֥תַן לִ֖⁠י יְהוָ֑ה
5.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could put this information first in the sentence, as the UST does.
See how you translated the term “throne” in 17:12. Alternate translation: [to be the king of the kingdom of Yahweh over Israel]

David considers Yahweh to be the true king of Israel, so it is the **kingdom of Yahweh**. He understands the earthly king to be Yahweh’s representative. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to be the king of Israel, as Yahweh’s representative]

6.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔⁠י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בִנְ⁠ךָ֔ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה בֵיתִ֖⁠י וַ⁠חֲצֵרוֹתָ֑⁠י כִּי־בָחַ֨רְתִּי ב֥⁠וֹ לִ⁠י֙ לְ⁠בֵ֔ן וַ⁠אֲנִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶה־לּ֥⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָֽב
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And he told me that my son Solomon would be the one to build his house and his courts, since he had chosen him for himself as a son, and for his part, he would be a father to him]

6.q: שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בִנְ⁠ךָ֔ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה בֵיתִ֖⁠י וַ⁠חֲצֵרוֹתָ֑⁠י כִּי־בָחַ֨רְתִּי ב֥⁠וֹ לִ⁠י֙ לְ⁠בֵ֔ן
6.note: tIf it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since I have chosen Solomon your son for myself as a son, he, he will build my house and my courts]

If it would not be natural in your language for both the name **Solomon** and the pronoun **he** to be the subjects of the verb **build**, you could express this in another way. Alternate translation: [As for Solomon your son, he, he will build]
See how you translated the same expression in 22:10. Alternate translation: [he will be the one to build]
See how you translated the same expression in 22:10. Alternate translation: [and for my part, I will be a father to him]

7.q: וַ⁠הֲכִינוֹתִ֥י אֶת־מַלְכוּת֖⁠וֹ עַד־לְ⁠עוֹלָ֑ם אִם־יֶחֱזַ֗ק לַ⁠עֲשׂ֛וֹת מִצְוֺתַ֥⁠י וּ⁠מִשְׁפָּטַ֖⁠י כַּ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
7.note: If you decided in the previous verse to translate this so that there would not be a quotation within a quotation, you can continue doing that here. Alternate translation: [He told me that he would establish his kingdom to forever if he was strong to do his commands and his judgments, as this day]

The author is using the strength that is necessary to do something continuously to represent doing something continuously. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he continually obeys]

The terms **commands** and **judgments** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all of my laws]

Yahweh is using the term **day** to refer to a specific time, the present time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as at present] or [as he is doing now]

8.note: See how you translated the expression “And now” in 17:7.

The author is using **eyes** to represent sight. Alternate translation: [in the sight of all of Israel, the assembly of Yahweh] or [I charge you, with all of you Israelites, who are Yahweh’s assembly, as witnesses]
The author is using **ears** to represent hearing. Alternate translation: [and in the hearing of our God] or [and also with our God as a witness]

The terms **keep** and **seek** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [earnestly obey]

9.note: David is speaking of himself in the third person as **your father** because he is giving Solomon a solemn admonition. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my God]

9.q: וְ⁠עָבְדֵ֗⁠הוּ בְּ⁠לֵ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ וּ⁠בְ⁠נֶ֣פֶשׁ חֲפֵצָ֔ה כִּ֤י כָל־לְבָבוֹת֙ דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠כָל־יֵ֥צֶר מַחֲשָׁב֖וֹת מֵבִ֑ין
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [and since Yahweh is seeking all hearts and is understanding every intention of thoughts, serve him with a whole heart and with a willing soul]

Here the **heart** represents a person’s desires and the **soul** represents a person’s resolve. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [wholeheartedly and enthusiastically]

The author is speaking of human **hearts** as if they were a container or an enclosed space that Yahweh could search to see what was inside. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh knows what each person desires]

The author is using the possessive form to describe an **intention** that a person would have in his **thoughts**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [everything that a person is thinking about because he intends to do it]

The expression **will be found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you will find him]

10.q: רְאֵ֣ה ׀ עַתָּ֗ה כִּֽי־יְהוָ֛ה בָּ֧חַר בְּ⁠ךָ֛ לִ⁠בְנֽוֹת־בַּ֥יִת לַ⁠מִּקְדָּ֖שׁ
10.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since Yahweh has chosen you to build a house as a sanctuary, see, now]
David is speaking as if he wants Solomon to **See** something. He means that he wants him to consider it carefully and appreciate its significance. Alternate translation: [Consider this carefully]

The verbs **Be strong** and **act** together express a single idea. The verb **Be strong** tells in what way David wants Solomon to **act**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [Act determinedly]

11.q: הָ⁠אוּלָם֩ וְֽ⁠אֶת־בָּ֨תָּ֜י⁠ו וְ⁠גַנְזַכָּ֧י⁠ו וַ⁠עֲלִיֹּתָ֛י⁠ו וַ⁠חֲדָרָ֥י⁠ו הַ⁠פְּנִימִ֖ים
11.note: In each instance in this verse, the pronoun **its** refers to the temple. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the porch of the temple and its houses and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its inner rooms]

The author is using the term **houses** to mean “buildings.” There was a main temple building and an addition, as 1 Kings 6:5–10 describes. The entire temple complex was considered to be a place where Yahweh was especially present. Alternate translation: [and its buildings]

The author assumes that readers will understand what he means by **its upper rooms**. However, interpreters are no longer certain what this phrase describes. This is an architectural detail of the temple that the author of 1 Kings does not mention. Some interpreters suggest that there were rooms inside the temple above the Holy of Holies. Other interpreters understand this phrase to describe the topmost rooms of the annex that surrounded the temple. But since the identity of these **rooms** is uncertain, we recommend that you use a general expression, as the UST does.

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **house**, in this case meaning a large room in the temple, that would characterized by it being a place where there was a **covering** over the Box of Yahweh, in the form of the wings of the two cherubs. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the room where the cherub’s wings would cover the Box of Yahweh]

The **house of the covering**, also known as the inner sanctuary, Holy of Holies, or Most Holy Place, was one of the **inner rooms** of the temple. (The other was the “nave” or Holy Place.) If this would not be clear from the word **and**, you may want to use a different connecting word. Alternate translation: [and its inner rooms, including the house of the covering]

12.note: The author is using this common expression of his culture to mean that God’s Spirit had inspired David to envision all the things he describes. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the Spirit had put in his mind] or [the Spirit had inspired him to envision]
See how you translated the same expression in 26:20. Alternate translation: [the gifts people had dedicated] or [the votive offerings]

14.note: The author is using **service and service** as a common expression of his culture to mean “various kinds of service.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, for both instances in this verse, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the vessels for this and that task] or [the vessels for various kinds of service]

14.q: לְ⁠כֹ֨ל כְּלֵ֤י הַ⁠כֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּ⁠מִשְׁקָ֔ל לְ⁠כָל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדָ֥ה וַ⁠עֲבוֹדָֽה
14.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [for silver by weight for silver for all of the vessels of service and service]

16.note: The author is using **for table and table** as a common expression of his culture to mean “for each table.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. (See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of why there would be more than one table in the temple for the bread of the arrangement.) Alternate translation: [for each of the tables for the bread of the arrangement]

17.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and gold by weight for the forks and the basins and the pitchers of pure gold]

The author is using **for bowl and bowl** as a common expression of his culture to mean “for each bowl.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, for each instance of this expression in this verse, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [specifying the weight for each bowl]

18.note: The author is using this possessive form not to describe a chariot that belonged to these cherubs but to describe these **cherubs** as constituting a **chariot** for Yahweh. (The Israelites envisioned Yahweh as seated upon these cherubs, as if they were his throne, the way someone would sit in a chariot. Psalm 99:1 says, for example, “Yahweh reigns … sitting above the cherubs.”) If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the gold cherubs that were like a chariot in which Yahweh sat]

The author assumes that readers will understand that by **spreading out**, he is referring to these cherub statues spreading out their wings. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for spreading out their wings]

19.note: This verse is a direct quotation from David. It continues his address to Solomon in verses 9–10. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [And David told Solomon further, “Everything is in writing]

Here, **hand** represents the control or influence of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from Yahweh’s influence on me] or [as Yahweh has guided me to write it]

20.note: The terms **strong** and **courageous** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Be very strong and act]
See how you translated the expression “Be strong and act” in 28:10. Alternate translation: [Act very determinedly]

20.q: אַל־תִּירָ֖א וְ⁠אַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֱלֹהַ⁠י֙ עִמָּ֔⁠ךְ
20.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since Yahweh God, my God, is with you, may you not fear, and may you not be dismayed]

These two statements mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [He will certainly not abandon you]

21.note: While David does want to focus Solomon’s attention on what he is about to say, in this context he also seems to be using the term **behold** literally, to mean that Solomon should look for encouragement at the **priests** and **Levites** who are ready to assume their duties. (While the author does not say specifically in v. 1 that they were present, this verse indicates that they were.) Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And here are]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:10. Alternate translation: [and every willing one with wisdom for all of the service will help you in all of the work]

David is using the adjective **willing** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. The ULT indicates this by supplying the word **one**. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [volunteer]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the leaders and all of the people will be with you for all of your ways] or [and the leaders and all of the people will help you for all of your ways]

David is speaking of the various tasks that Solomon will need to complete as if they were **ways** or paths that he would need to walk along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the leaders and all of the people will help you with every task you need to complete]
